chapter_theme: Attaining the holy feet (திருவடிப் பேறு): the guru, Nandi, lays his hand and his feet on the disciple's head, heart and eyes, removes the forms of the self and makes him Siva beyond words; the knowledge of the holy feet is itself Siva-hood, release and every mantra, medicine and path.
structure_note: 1590 to 1597 narrate the speaker's initiation in the first person: the touch, the feet on the head, the ending of forms and words. 1598 to 1604 generalize: what the knowledge of the feet does, what neglecting them brings, and the feet as all things.

1590.reading: As love rose in harmony, the guru red as Siva came and placed his hand on my head, so that I went to the Lord who rises with tenderness within the bond, and the guru's joyful feet came gladly into my heart.
1590.nuance: சென்னி கை வைக்க, placing the hand on the head, is traditionally taken as initiation by touch (hasta-diksha). பாசத்துள் ஏக is unclear: going within the bond, or the bond going.

1591.reading: When he gave his feet, our Lord took my head; he gave me the strength of knowledge that is a sword and, leaving me with 'rule without end of release', set a crown on me in grace's glory and gave me the world.
1591.nuance: தலைதந்த can mean the Lord gave headship or took the head (the ego) in exchange; the exchange of feet for head is a common devotional image. பாடு and பார்வந்து தந்தது are unclear.

1592.reading: Becoming himself, coming into my true form, he removed the four forms that had arisen; good Nandi, who ruled me giving the other seal, first crowned me with his feet and established me: this is true.
1592.nuance: சொரூபம், the self's own form, and the four சொரூபங்கள் are technical; they may be the four states preceding the true form. முத்திரை may be a ritual gesture given in initiation or a seal of identity.

1593.reading: Word ended, feeling ended, soul and supreme ended; like water without waves, he did away even with becoming Siva and set me in the true form beyond the shoreless four beginning with being; we passed beyond words.
1593.nuance: சிவமாதல் தீர்த்து, ending even the becoming-Siva, goes past any state still named. சத்தாதி நான்கு (the four beginning with sat) are unclear. Sengalvaraya notes a near-identical opening in Kandar Alangaram 61.

1594.reading: The guru took the soul's three forms and took the rare reality as a seal; Nandi, the feet of the great Lord, wordless, took me there and saved me so that I melted.
1594.nuance: உயிர் முச்சொரூபம், the soul's three forms, and பொருள் முத்திரை are technical terms I can't fix.

1595.reading: In the great bliss beyond speech, he made me, freed of stain, Siva and made me die; the flawless light took over the three debts and, so that the fame that had come died away, gave his feet and abides.
1595.nuance: மாள்வித்து, causing to die, is the death of the self. கடன் மூன்று (three debts) may be the three malas or the three traditional debts; வாச்ச புகழ் மாள, the fame that came dying away, is unclear.

1596.reading: How Nandi, the supreme, who set his feet in my heart, my eyes and my head, gave me the goal, how he showed the truth and how he set the rule cannot be spoken.
1596.nuance: Heart, eyes and head are the places of the guru's touch and gaze in initiation as tradition reads it; the verse ends, like 1593, in what cannot be said.

1597.reading: Placing his holy feet on my head and looking with grace, I saw great Nandi who took a great form, the king, our king, in the form of the guru, so that the path to the womb was drained away.
1597.nuance: கருவழி வாற்றிட, draining the womb-path, is ending rebirth. The guru's form and Nandi's great form are one in what the speaker saw.

1598.reading: Knowledge of the holy feet makes one Siva; knowledge of the holy feet brings one to Sivaloka; knowledge of the holy feet frees one from the prison of impurity; knowledge of the holy feet is itself firm siddhi and release.
1598.nuance: திருவடி ஞானம் opens every line. It may mean knowledge of the feet or the knowledge that the feet are; the verse lets both stand.

1599.reading: If one does not do as he set above, the deeds to come will turn a mind dazed by delusion into illusion; this is how the sky-dweller of spreading light, with milk on his head, set his feet and made me bear them.
1599.nuance: மேல்வைத்தவாறு (as he set above, or as set out above) and மேல்வினை (later karma, or karma on top) play on மேல். பால் on the head may be the moon or the Ganga. The link between the two halves is unclear.

1600.reading: I gained the shade called the anklet-bearing lotus holy feet; the First Lord within the fire that tall Mal could not know will also break apart the nest of my life where the coil dwells.
1600.nuance: நெடுமால் அறியா அழல் recalls the story of the column of fire whose end Vishnu could not find. குழல் சேரும் கூடு (the nest where the coil or tube joins) is taken as the body with kundalini or the central channel; breaking it may mean release from the body.

1601.reading: Crowned kings rule the three worlds, but the bliss of those who are kings of the feet has no measure, if you ask; the gods who stood as crowned kings stood free of fault as subjects of the Lord.
1601.nuance: முடிமன்னர் and அடிமன்னர், kings of the crown and kings of the feet, set head against feet: kingship at the Lord's feet outranks the gods' own crowns.

1602.reading: I set his feet within my mind so as not to go by the senses that burn falsely; worn out, I turned away the two whirling deeds and knew the true honey, the end of the Veda.
1602.nuance: இருவினை, the two deeds, are good and bad karma, both binding. புலன் வழி, the way of the senses, is the opposite of keeping the feet in mind. மெய்த்தேன் puns on true honey and 'I attained truth'.

1603.reading: The sages of old placed on their heads the Lord's two feet, to which one may cling; this is the principle of those who stand joined to the path of those who dwell in the ancient flood of bliss on earth.
1603.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are compressed: படிசார்ந்த (come down to earth, or in due order) and குடிசார் நெறி (the path of the household of devotees) are uncertain.

1604.reading: What is mantra, what is great medicine, what is tantra, what are gifts, what is beauty and what is the pure path: it is our Father Lord's pair of feet.
1604.nuance: தானங்கள் may be gifts (dana) or holy places (sthana). The verse folds every religious means, ritual and textual, into the feet.

links.note: Both are four-line anaphoras on திருவடி. 138 makes the feet Sivam, Sivaloka, the path and the refuge; 1598 makes knowledge of the feet the agent that makes one Siva, brings to Sivaloka, frees from mala and is release.

Both use the same words for the end state: beyond word (உரையற்று), without waves (திரையற்ற), shoreless (கரையற்ற). 134 describes those who understand the teacher's word; 1593 is the speaker's own passing beyond words.
Both narrate the guru placing his feet on the speaker's head: in 113 as a guard that melts him and removes the verdigris, in 1597 so that the path back to the womb is drained.
Both join the head to the Lord's feet: the Kural calls a head that does not bow to them useless, Tirumular says the old sages set the feet on their heads.
Both say the two deeds, good and bad, cease for one devoted to the Lord: the Kural through praising him, Tirumular through holding his feet in the mind.
Both make a death of the self the way to become Siva: 1907's living who have died to the three malas, 1595's speaker made Siva and made to die in the bliss beyond speech.

1591 narrates the moment: when the Lord gave his feet (தாடந்த போதே) he took the head, gave the sword-strength of knowledge and the rule of release; 2049 lists what the true guru does by giving his feet (தாள்தந்து, four times): protects, grants self-knowledge, takes the soul beyond the tattvas, quells the bonds. 2049 is the doctrine of which 1591 is the first-person event.

1592 says good Nandi first crowned him with his feet (தானடி முற்சூட்டி) and established him; 89, in Tirumular's account of his own history, says Nandi gave release and set his good feet on my head (அடியேன் சிரத்தினில் நற்பதமும் அளித்தான்). The feet set on the disciple's head as the sign of initiation is the same figure in both, and 89 places in the prefatory history the event 1592 describes in its technical terms.

1596 says Nandi set his feet in my heart, my eyes and my head (இதயத்தும் நாட்டத்தும் என்றன் சிரத்தும்) and how he did it cannot be told; 73 says Tirumular placed Nandi's feet on his head and set them within his mind (நான்தலை மேற்கொண்டு புந்தியின் உள்ளே புகப்பெய்து) before telling the Agama. The feet on the head and within the mind appear in both; in 73 the disciple takes them up, in 1596 the guru sets them.

372 tells how Brahma and Mal, each saying 'I am the Lord', faced the Supreme spread out as fire and searched for Hara's feet crying out; 1600 says 'I gained the shade of the anklet-bearing lotus feet' of the First Lord within the fire tall Mal could not know (நெடுமால் அறியா அழல்). The feet the gods could not reach by searching are, for the devotee, a shade he has entered.

1601 sets crowned kings (முடிமன்னர்) against kings of the feet (அடிமன்னர்) and says the crowned gods stand as subjects of the Lord; 2785 calls the Lord's flower feet the great jewel that sits on the crowns of the crowned gods (தாமுடி வானவர் தம்முடி மேலுறை மாமணி). Both place the feet on top of the gods' crowns, so head and foot reverse rank.

Kural 7 says that except for those who reach the feet of the incomparable one it is hard to remove the mind's anxiety (தாள்சேர்ந்தார்க் கல்லால் மனக்கவலை மாற்றல் அரிது); 1604 says the Lord's pair of feet is mantra, great medicine (மாமருந்து), tantra, gifts and the pure path. The Kural makes the feet the one remedy; Tirumular extends it so that every religious means is the feet.

source_issues: 1591: lines 3 and 4 (வீடந்தம் இன்றியே யாள்கென, பாடின் முடிவைத்துப் பார்வந்து தந்ததே) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1603: lines 3 and 4 are compressed and unclear.
